functionality: Beacon defines a Test Contract Index with feature identity, truth refs, runtime/docs line, lane membership, AC/TC/test/evidence mapping, status, and reason codes.
Beacon defines canonical lanes for feature release-facing tests, current runtime contracts, generated surface sync, compatibility contracts, and legacy snapshots.
Release-facing single tests must map to AC/TC and evidence or declare a generated-surface contract reason.
Doctor support commands own building and verifying the test contract index; no new public lifecycle stage is introduced.
QA guidance and execution preserve AC order, evidence pack, coverage current/gap, continue decision, severe blocker stop, repair handoff, `beacon help` resume, and next-round backfill.
Release scorecard and strict gate consume lane status and block on missing, stale, failed, or unclassified release-facing evidence.
Generated skill, metadata, command, context, and agent surfaces are classified under `generated_surface_sync` and can block release when drift affects delivery truth.
Historical snapshot failures are routed to `legacy_snapshot` or test evolution backlog unless explicitly promoted to `compatibility_contract`.
Beacon skills instruct agents to use contract-lane verification and avoid unclassified full-suite release claims.
Deep test deltas are adopted through `test-case` or supplemental `qa`; deep remains a support surface and does not execute QA.
Freezing v1.4.2 requirements does not change current runtime release line, docs default line, or package version.
When test contract governance blocks delivery, Beacon provides reason codes and repair or resume routes through existing support surfaces.
